andhraPradesh.headline: Recent downpour shifts 11 Andhra Pradesh districts into normal rainfall category
facts: APWRIMS recorded 379.06 mm of state rainfall against a 539.2 mm normal through September 25, a 29.7% deficit.
The New Indian Express reported 68.64 mm of rain over two days, against a normal 11.59 mm for that period.
The report said 11 of the State’s 28 districts had moved into the normal rainfall category; Annamayya remained in the large-deficit category at 62.09%.
The rainfall improvement followed the deep depression’s passage near Kalingapatnam on September 23–24.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: The listed coverage already tracked the Kharif rainfall-deficit recovery. Today: new reporting on September 26 described a two-day downpour and 11 districts moving into the normal category. Official APWRIMS data through September 25 recorded a 29.7% statewide deficit, while the newspaper reported a different cumulative percentage; the figures may reflect different reporting bases.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Indian monsoon, rainfall variability, drought and agricultural vulnerability
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: APWRIMS is the state rainfall dashboard; distinguish a short-period rainfall excess from the cumulative seasonal deficit.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how rainfall extremes can ease seasonal water stress while simultaneously increasing flood and crop-damage risks.
andhraPradesh.apLink: This is a direct AP link: district rainfall classifications and statewide Kharif rainfall conditions.

> Exam angle: Distinguish short-period rainfall from the cumulative seasonal deficit, and note the **11 of 28** district shift.

andhraPradesh.headline: New district-level reports detail crop and road damage from heavy rain
facts: A September 26 report said 9,882 hectares of paddy were inundated across 18 mandals in Kakinada district.
The same report cited damage to 155 hectares of cotton, 111 hectares of black gram and 72 hectares of maize in Kakinada, affecting 8,552 farmers.
It reported 133 km of damaged R&B roads in Kakinada district.
The report also cited 5,381 acres of inundated crops in Eluru district and about 13,000 acres under water in East Godavari district.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: Coverage on September 25 concerned crop-loss assessment following the heavy rain. Today: district-level reporting added specific estimates for inundated crops, affected farmers and damaged roads. These are reported damage figures, not a final government loss assessment or announced compensation.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Agricultural risk, crop-loss assessment and disaster-response administration
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Separate preliminary inundation and damage estimates from a completed crop-loss enumeration or compensation decision.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how flood damage to crops and rural roads affects farm livelihoods, market access and disaster-relief priorities.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The reported damage figures concern Kakinada, Eluru, East Godavari, Srikakulam and other Andhra Pradesh districts.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh reports power-network restoration after deep-depression impacts
facts: The State’s Special Chief Secretary for Energy said restoration followed the deep depression’s landfall near Kalingapatnam on September 23–24.
APTRANSCO and the State’s three distribution companies coordinated restoration measures.
The report said teams had re-energised 18 feeders and two critical power transformers, while work on remaining infrastructure was nearing completion.
Floodwater inundated a 132 kV substation in Visakhapatnam; the report also described repairs to transmission lines in several districts.
andhraPradesh.summary: On September 26, the State energy administration reported progress restoring electricity infrastructure affected by heavy rain and strong winds. The report described partial restoration and continuing work, not full completion of all repairs.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Electricity transmission and distribution; disaster-resilient critical infrastructure
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: APTRANSCO is the State transmission utility; APEPDCL, APSPDCL and APCPDCL are the distribution companies named in the restoration report.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess the importance of utility coordination, emergency control rooms and resilient substations in maintaining essential services during extreme-weather events.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The restoration involved Andhra Pradesh’s power utilities and affected infrastructure in Visakhapatnam and other State districts.

national.headline: Foundation stone laid for 150-tonne-per-day port-based e-methanol plant at Kandla
facts: The ₹2,300-crore project is a joint initiative of Deendayal Port Authority and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd.
Planned total capacity is 150 tonnes per day, in phases of 50 and 100 tonnes per day.
The plant is to use renewable power, water and biogenic CO₂ to produce e-methanol for ships on the Asia-Europe trade corridor.
The foundation stone was laid at Kandla, Gujarat, on 26 September 2026; the project is at foundation-stone stage.
The Union government identifies it as India’s first port-based e-methanol production facility.
AP link: No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The foundation stone was laid at Deendayal Port Authority in Kandla for a port-based facility intended to supply lower-carbon fuel to shipping. The government describes it as India’s first such port-based plant; it is not yet operational.
national.staticLink: Green hydrogen and derivatives; decarbonisation of maritime transport; ports and energy transition.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The project at Kandla is planned to produce e-methanol from renewable power, water and biogenic CO₂, with a stated capacity of 150 tonnes per day.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how green marine fuels and port-linked energy infrastructure can support India’s climate commitments and create new export opportunities.

- **Capacity:** Planned total of **150 tonnes per day**, in phases of **50 tonnes per day** and **100 tonnes per day**
- **Process:** Renewable power, water and biogenic **CO₂** for e-methanol production
- **Use:** Fuel for ships on the **Asia-Europe trade corridor**

# 2. Location and status
- **Where:** **Kandla, Gujarat**, at **Deendayal Port Authority**

national.headline: India’s women retain Asian Games kabaddi gold, defeating Iran 37–34
facts: India defeated Iran 37–34 in the women’s kabaddi final at the 2026 Asian Games.
The final was played in Nagoya, Japan, on 26 September 2026.
India secured its second consecutive Asian Games women’s kabaddi gold.
The score at half-time was 22–16 in India’s favour.

national.headline: IIT Madras deep-tech venture fund announces first close and startup selections
facts: IIT Madras Research Park and Unicorn India Ventures launched the IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund I for deep-tech startups.
The fund targets a corpus of ₹600–1,000 crore and is intended to provide patient capital, technical support and mentorship.
IIT Madras announced the fund’s first close and selected startups at the IIT Madras Alumni Association’s Sangam 2026 in Bengaluru.
Akashvani reported a first close of ₹453 crore and ₹55 crore invested in four startups on the launch day.

national.headline: CSIR-NIScPR launches popular science magazines in five Indian languages
facts: Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh launched five magazines on CSIR’s 85th Foundation Day.
The publications—Vigyan Velugu (Telugu), Ariviyal Arikkaiyalar (Tamil), Vidnyan Kshitij (Marathi), Bigyan Brittanto (Bengali) and Bigyan Lahar (Assamese)—are published by CSIR-NIScPR.
The stated aim is to widen access to science communication in Indian languages.
Vigyan Velugu is a Telugu-language edition relevant to Telugu-speaking readers, including in Andhra Pradesh; the announcement does not specify an AP-specific rollout.
AP link: Telugu-language science communication is relevant to AP readers; no state-specific rollout was announced.
national.summary: CSIR-NIScPR expanded its popular-science publishing portfolio with five language editions, including Telugu, on 26 September. The initiative is intended to make scientific knowledge more accessible to readers in their languages.

national.headline: ECI directs home visits to collect documents from electors issued SIR notices
facts: At its 26 September meeting, the Election Commission directed Booth Level Officers to visit the homes of people issued notices during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and collect supporting documents.
The documents are to be uploaded on ECINet for decision by the Electoral Registration Officer.
The Commission said personal hearings would not generally be required; exceptional hearings should preferably be online, and an elector may authorise an adult family member to attend.
District Election Officers were asked to arrange help desks or camps, as needed, for people including migrant workers, homeless people and residents of night shelters.
AP link: No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The Election Commission announced procedural measures for electors issued notices during the ongoing SIR. These include home-based document collection by BLOs and hearings only in exceptional cases, preferably online.
national.staticLink: Election Commission of India; electoral-roll revision; voter registration and representation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Under the ECI’s 26 September directions, BLOs collect documents at home from SIR notice recipients and upload them to ECINet for ERO consideration.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how administrative convenience, due process and accessible grievance mechanisms can be balanced during electoral-roll revision.

national.headline: Special Campaign 6 review records preparatory work across 84 central ministries and departments
facts: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) is the nodal department for Special Campaign 6.
The preparatory phase runs from 16–30 September 2026; the implementation phase is scheduled for 2–31 October 2026.
A 26 September review meeting represented 84 ministries/departments, their PSUs and field offices, with officials joining from more than 500 locations.
Preparatory work includes identifying pending references, planning cleanliness drives and assessing e-waste for disposal.
The campaign is monitored through a dedicated portal; PIB reported 1,039 campaign-related tweets and 54 PIB statements by 26 September.
AP link: No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: DARPG reviewed Special Campaign 6’s preparatory progress on 26 September, ahead of its October implementation phase. The campaign covers cleanliness, disposal of pending matters, e-waste management and records and office-space management across central government offices.
national.staticLink: Administrative reforms; cleanliness in public offices; pendency reduction and records management.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Special Campaign 6’s preparatory phase is 16–30 September 2026, followed by implementation from 2–31 October 2026; DARPG is the nodal department.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how time-bound, portal-monitored campaigns can improve cleanliness, records management and responsiveness in public administration.

national.headline: World Tourism Day backgrounder highlights India’s tourism statistics and planned digital initiatives
facts: World Tourism Day 2026 is observed on 27 September under the theme “Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism”; the host country is El Salvador.
The PIB backgrounder reports tourism’s contribution at 5.22% of India’s GDP and 8.46 crore jobs in 2023–24.
For 2025, it reports 428.55 crore domestic tourist visits, 2.53 crore foreign tourist visits and ₹2,76,831 crore in foreign-exchange earnings from tourism.

international.headline: India and GCC review cooperation plan as FTA negotiations advance
facts: The India-GCC Troika Ministerial Meeting was held in New York on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly session.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar co-chaired the meeting with Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani.
Participants reviewed implementation of the India-GCC Joint Action Plan 2024–2028, covering areas including trade, investment, energy, food security, health and technology.
The sides welcomed the launch of India-GCC Free Trade Agreement negotiations after finalising their Terms of Reference in February 2026.
The ministers agreed to hold the second India-GCC Joint Ministerial Meeting for Strategic Dialogue at an early date; the FTA was not concluded at this meeting.
international.summary: At the 25 September meeting, India and GCC representatives reviewed the 2024–2028 cooperation plan and welcomed the start of FTA negotiations. The meeting linked India’s economic and energy ties with Gulf states to broader cooperation, including food security and technology.
international.staticLink: India’s foreign relations; regional organisations; free trade agreements and economic diplomacy.
international.prelimsTakeaway: GCC comprises Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE; distinguish the launch of FTA negotiations from a signed or concluded FTA.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how India-GCC cooperation can diversify beyond energy trade while deepening economic integration, food security and people-to-people ties.

international.headline: China and United States announce AI communication channel and trade understandings after leaders’ meeting
facts: China’s official readout, published 26 September, said Xi Jinping’s 23–25 September state visit to the United States produced eight stated deliverables and understandings.
The countries agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel for AI incidents and a China-U.S. AI Dialogue; the next exchange was stated to be due in November 2026.
The White House said the countries reached consensus on recommendations for more favourable tariff treatment for $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction.

The White House said the two sides operationalised Boards of Trade and Investment; the Chinese readout referred to a planned memorandum of understanding on military crisis communication that was still to be concluded.
These announcements describe understandings and planned mechanisms; they do not establish that the military crisis-communication MOU had been signed.
international.summary: On 26 September, China published its account of outcomes from the leaders’ visit, including an AI incident channel and a bilateral AI dialogue. The White House separately described trade-treatment recommendations for $30 billion of goods in each direction and the operation of bilateral trade and investment boards; the announced military MOU remained prospective.
international.staticLink: Bilateral diplomacy; international trade and tariffs; global AI governance and risk management.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Separate announced dialogue and communication mechanisms from a signed treaty; note the two official accounts’ descriptions of the trade outcome.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how crisis-communication mechanisms and AI dialogue between major powers could contribute to global technology governance while trade negotiations continue.

- **What:** **China’s** official readout, published on **26 September 2026**, stated **eight** deliverables and understandings from **Xi Jinping’s** state visit to the **United States**, **23–25 September 2026**
- **Status:** **ANNOUNCED**

# 2. AI and trade outcomes
- **AI mechanisms:** Agreement to establish a bilateral **AI incidents communication channel** and a **China-U.S. AI Dialogue**
- **Next exchange:** **November 2026**
- **Trade:** The **White House** said the countries reached consensus on recommendations for more favourable tariff treatment for **$30 billion** of non-sensitive goods in **each direction**
- **Boards:** The **White House** said the two sides operationalised **Boards of Trade and Investment**
- **Military crisis communication:** The **Chinese readout** referred to a planned memorandum of understanding (**MoU**) that was still to be concluded
- ⚠ **Trap:** Announced dialogue and communication mechanisms are not a signed treaty; the military crisis-communication **MoU remained prospective**, not signed.

# 3. Exam focus
- **Context:** Bilateral diplomacy, international trade and global **AI** governance
> Exam angle: APPSC may ask about the announced AI mechanisms, the **$30 billion** trade-treatment recommendations in each direction, or the prospective status of the military crisis-communication MoU.

international.headline: International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons observed on 26 September
facts: The United Nations observes 26 September as the International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons.
The UN General Assembly declared the day through resolution 68/32 in 2013.
The observance aims to raise public awareness of the threat posed by nuclear weapons and the need for their elimination.
The UN identifies nuclear disarmament as a priority within its disarmament agenda.
international.summary: The annual UN observance calls attention to nuclear risks and the objective of global nuclear disarmament. It provides a useful link to multilateral disarmament, non-proliferation and international peace and security.
international.staticLink: Nuclear disarmament; non-proliferation; United Nations and multilateral diplomacy.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the date, 26 September, and UN General Assembly resolution 68/32 (2013).
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the gap between the international commitment to nuclear disarmament and the continuing challenge of building effective, inclusive arms-control arrangements.

sources.title: International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons

international.notes:
# 1. Observance
- **Name:** **International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons**
- **Date:** **26 September** each year
- **Status:** **ONGOING**

# 2. UN basis and purpose
- **Declared by:** **United Nations General Assembly** through **Resolution 68/32** in **2013**
- **Objective:** Raise public awareness of the threat posed by **nuclear weapons** and the need for their elimination
- **UN priority:** **Nuclear disarmament** is a priority within the **UN disarmament agenda**

# 3. Exam focus
- **Context:** Nuclear disarmament, non-proliferation and international peace and security
> Exam angle: APPSC may test the observance date, its full name and the **2013 UN General Assembly Resolution 68/32**.

international.headline: Demi Vollering wins the women’s elite road race at the UCI Road World Championships
facts: The women’s elite road race at the 2026 UCI Road World Championships was held in Montréal, Canada, over 180.1 km.
The Netherlands’ Demi Vollering won the race in 4:45:09.
Poland’s Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney finished second with the same recorded time; Italy’s Elisa Longo Borghini was third, four seconds behind.
The result is a final race result; no AP athlete connection was established.
international.summary: Vollering won the women’s elite road race on 26 September in Montréal. Niewiadoma-Phinney finished second and Longo Borghini third in the 180.1 km event.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the India-GCC Troika Ministerial Meeting, consider the following statements:
1. The meeting reviewed implementation of the India-GCC Joint Action Plan 2024–2028.
2. India and the GCC concluded their Free Trade Agreement at the meeting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
mcqs.explanation: The ministers reviewed the 2024–2028 Joint Action Plan and welcomed the launch of FTA negotiations; the FTA was not concluded at the meeting.

mcqs.question: Which of the following mechanisms did China and the United States agree to establish for AI-related engagement?
options: A bilateral communication channel for AI incidents and a China-U.S. AI Dialogue
A jointly administered global AI regulator
A permanent international court for AI disputes
A common tariff authority for artificial-intelligence services
mcqs.explanation: The stated understandings included a bilateral channel for AI incidents and a China-U.S. AI Dialogue, with the next exchange due in November 2026.

mcqs.question: The United Nations observes the International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons on 26 September. The day was declared through which resolution?
options: UN General Assembly resolution 68/32
UN Security Council resolution 68/32
UN General Assembly resolution 81/26
UN Security Council resolution 81/26
mcqs.explanation: The UN General Assembly declared the observance through resolution 68/32 in 2013.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the e-methanol project at Kandla:
1. It is a joint initiative of Deendayal Port Authority and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd.
2. Its planned total capacity is 150 tonnes per day, in phases of 50 and 100 tonnes per day.
3. On 26 September 2026, it was reported as operational.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
mcqs.explanation: The project is a joint initiative with planned capacity of 150 tonnes per day. Its foundation stone had been laid, so it was not operational.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Election Commission’s direction concerning electors issued SIR notices?
options: Booth Level Officers are to visit homes and collect supporting documents for uploading on ECINet.
All electors issued notices must attend an in-person hearing at the Election Commission’s headquarters.
Documents must be submitted only through a state government portal.
District Election Officers were directed to suspend help desks and camps.
mcqs.explanation: The Commission directed home visits by Booth Level Officers and uploading of documents on ECINet for the Electoral Registration Officer’s decision.

mcqs.question: Which statement about Special Campaign 6 is correct?
options: Its preparatory phase runs from 16–30 September 2026, and implementation is scheduled for 2–31 October 2026.
Its implementation phase began on 16 September and ends on 30 September 2026.
It is coordinated by the Election Commission of India.
Its preparatory work excludes assessment of e-waste for disposal.
mcqs.explanation: DARPG is the nodal department; the preparatory phase runs from 16–30 September and the implementation phase is scheduled for 2–31 October.

mcqs.question: According to the reported AP rainfall figures through 25 September, which statement is correct?
options: State rainfall was 379.06 mm against a 539.2 mm normal, a 29.7% deficit.
State rainfall was 539.2 mm against a 379.06 mm normal, a 29.7% surplus.
State rainfall was 68.64 mm against a 11.59 mm normal for the entire period through 25 September.
Annamayya was reported to have moved into the normal rainfall category.
mcqs.explanation: APWRIMS recorded 379.06 mm against a 539.2 mm normal through 25 September. Annamayya remained in the large-deficit category.

mcqs.question: Which agencies were reported to have coordinated Andhra Pradesh’s power-network restoration after the deep-depression impacts?
options: APTRANSCO and the State’s three distribution companies
The Election Commission and the State’s three distribution companies
Deendayal Port Authority and APTRANSCO
DARPG and the State’s three distribution companies
mcqs.explanation: APTRANSCO and the State’s three distribution companies coordinated restoration measures, including re-energising feeders and critical transformers.
